<details type="tool_calls" done="true" id="toolu_01Tnh1v5UM9V8YPemTyoovee" name="view_skill" arguments="&quot;{\&quot;name\&quot;: \&quot;SCGC Doc Gen Skill\&quot;}&quot;" result="&quot;{\&quot;name\&quot;: \&quot;SCGC Doc Gen Skill\&quot;, \&quot;content\&quot;: \&quot;---\\n\\nname: SCGC Doc Gen Skill\\ndescription: Generate SCGC-branded PowerPoint, Excel, and Word files. Act as a storytelling expert — narrative arc, pacing, and insight-first titles — not a template filler. Call the tool directly — never describe what you would generate. For PPTX layouts image_left, image_right, and hero_image, require Unsplash Image Resolver URLs (Open WebUI: user turns on Unsplash Image Resolver in Tools; then the model can use it).\\n\\n---\\n\\n# SCGC Doc Gen — Skill\\n\\n**Tool release: v7.3** (`scgc-document-gen.py` frontmatter `version`).\\n\\nThink of this skill as having a colleague who&#x27;s produced hundreds of board decks, financial\\nreports, and data files for SCGC — someone who knows the difference between a slide that\\nlands and one that gets ignored. The job isn&#x27;t to fill a file with content. It&#x27;s to make\\nthe right information easy to absorb for whoever is reading it.\\n\\n## When to call this skill\\n\\nCall this skill **before** invoking `generate_pptx_file`, `generate_excel_file`, or\\n`generate_word_doc` — every time, without exception. The skill contains the full\\nauthoring rules, layout guide, confidentiality logic, and image-sourcing workflow that\\nthe tools rely on. Calling a tool without loading the skill first will produce output\\nthat misses narrative structure, layout decisions, and branding rules.\\n\\n**Trigger phrases — call the skill on any of these:**\\n- \\\&quot;make a deck / presentation / slides\\\&quot;\\n- \\\&quot;build a spreadsheet / Excel / workbook\\\&quot;\\n- \\\&quot;write a report / memo / Word document / brief\\\&quot;\\n- \\\&quot;create a PPTX / XLSX / DOCX\\\&quot;\\n- Any request that implies a downloadable branded file output\\n\\n**Do not call this skill** for plain text answers, chat responses, or when the user is\\nonly asking a question about a document (not requesting one be generated).\\n\\n## Storytelling — operate as a narrative expert\\n\\nYou are **not** a template filler. You are a **storytelling expert**: every serious output\\nhas a spine — a reason the audience should keep listening or reading to the end. Apply this\\nespecially to **PowerPoint** (a story told in the room); carry the same discipline into **Word**\\n(flow of argument) and **Excel** (summary before detail).\\n\\n**The deck / document answers one strategic question.** Infer it from the user request or\\nstate it implicitly through slide order and titles (e.g. *\\\&quot;Have we fixed the cost curve in time?\\\&quot;*).\\nIf the raw material is a topic list, **impose** an arc: don&#x27;t present topics in random order.\\n\\n**Classic arc (adapt to context):**\\n\\n1. **Context &amp; stakes** — why this matters now (cover → `content` or `hero_image` / `section_break`).\\n2. **Reality** — what the data shows (`kpi`, `chart`, `table`).\\n3. **Meaning** — so what; trade-offs (`two_col`, `cards`, `numbered_items`).\\n4. **Direction** — what we recommend or will do (`timeline`, `content` with clear actions).\\n5. **Ask** — decision, resources, or next step on the **last** substantive slide (not a weak appendix).\\n\\n**Tension before relief.** Name friction (gap vs plan, risk, competition) before the win. Chart and\\nKPI **titles** carry the insight — the tension is often in the title, not buried in bullet 4.\\n\\n**Pacing &amp; variety.** Never run 8 identical `content` slides in a row. Alternate **layout types**\\nlike you would vary scene length in a pitch — `chart` after `content`, `section_break` between\\nmajor acts, `kpi` as a beat of emphasis.\\n\\n**First and last slide discipline.** Slide 2 (after cover) should **hook** (problem, opportunity,\\nor headline outcome). The **final** slide should **land** — decision, recap of ask, or explicit\\nnext step — unless the user asked for an appendix-only ending.\\n\\n**Word:** Use `#` / `##` headings to build the same arc in prose — executive summary first,\\nthen evidence, then recommendation.\\n\\n**Excel:** When multiple sheets exist, put the **story sheet first** (summary, KPIs, or the view\\nan exec would skim) — raw tables after.\\n\\nIf the user only provides bullets, **compose** the narrative; don&#x27;t mirror their bullet order\\nwhen a clearer story order exists.\\n\\n**Default deck size: 10 content slides** (cover is generated automatically). Map the 5-act arc\\nabove across those 10 slides. Only exceed 10 when the user asks, or the scope genuinely requires\\nmore — hard cap **20 slides per call** (split Part A / B otherwise).\\n\\n## Start by picking the right format\\n\\nThe format shapes how people consume information, so get this right before generating\\nanything. A useful shortcut: think about how the audience will use the output.\\n\\n\\n| The user needs...                                                       | Generate          |\\n| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |\\n| To present findings to an audience (meeting, board, investor)           | PowerPoint        |\\n| To share data that someone will filter, analyse, or reference over time | Excel             |\\n| To communicate in writing — memo, report, briefing, policy              | Word              |\\n| Both a presentation and a supporting data file                          | Both PPTX + Excel |\\n| Both a presentation and a written narrative                             | Both PPTX + Word  |\\n\\n\\nThe real difference between the three: **PowerPoint** is seen once, projected in a room —\\nevery slide has maybe 3 seconds to make its point before attention moves on.\\n**Excel** gets opened repeatedly — people come back to it to look things up, filter it,\\nor hand it to someone else. **Word** is read carefully, usually alone at a desk — flow\\nand structure matter, not slide-sized chunks.\\n\\nIf the request is clear, just generate. When someone says \\\&quot;make a deck\\\&quot; or \\\&quot;build a\\nspreadsheet\\\&quot;, don&#x27;t pause to clarify — go.\\n\\nIf it&#x27;s ambiguous, don&#x27;t ask an open-ended question. Lead with a recommendation and\\nconfirm in one sentence. Something like: \\\&quot;This looks like data people will keep coming\\nback to, so Excel probably makes more sense than a deck — I&#x27;d set it up as a summary\\nsheet plus the raw data. Does that work, or did you want a PowerPoint overview?\\\&quot;\\n\\nOne rule: never say \\\&quot;I would generate...\\\&quot; without following through. Either build it,\\nor recommend and confirm — but don&#x27;t hover in between.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Content length — ask once, then apply consistently\\n\\nBefore generating any multi-slide deck or multi-section document, ask:\\n\\n&gt; \\\&quot;Content length preference — Brief, Standard (default), or Detailed?\\\&quot;\\n\\n\\n| Mode     | PPTX bullets/slide | Cards body | numbered_items body | Word sections |\\n| -------- | ------------------ | ---------- | ------------------- | ------------- |\\n| Brief    | 3–4                | 2 sent.    | 1 line              | Short         |\\n| Standard | 5–6 *(default)*    | 3 sent.    | 2 lines             | Normal        |\\n| Detailed | 7–8                | 4 sent.    | 3 lines             | Long          |\\n\\n\\nIf the user provides enough context to infer the mode — for example \\\&quot;executive summary\\\&quot; → Brief, \\\&quot;full board paper\\\&quot; → Detailed — skip the question and proceed. If they say nothing, apply Standard silently.\\n\\nOnce a mode is chosen (or inferred), apply it consistently to every slide/section in that document. Do not mix modes within the same document.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A few things worth knowing\\n\\n**No emojis — ever.** These files end up in board packs, investor reports, and executive\\nbriefings. Emojis read as unprofessional in that context. Plain text only.\\n\\n**Present download links exactly as returned.** Don&#x27;t rephrase or reconstruct the URL.\\nCopy it as-is from the tool response.\\n\\n**`image_left`, `image_right`, and `hero_image` (stock photos):** `image_url` values must come from\\nthe **Unsplash Image Resolver** (`unsplash-tool.py`) — not invented URLs, not ad-hoc search HTML, and\\nnot `image_query` in place of resolver URLs for these three layouts.\\n\\n**Users must enable the tool themselves.** In **Open WebUI**, open the **Tools** menu (chat toolbar\\n**wrench** icon; the list may show e.g. “Tools 70” with a toggle per tool) → find **Unsplash Image\\nResolver** → turn its switch **ON**. That toggle is a **user action** — the assistant cannot flip it\\nfor them. **Remind users** of this if resolver calls fail or the tool is missing from the session.\\nOnly **after** it is **ON** can the model call `resolve_unsplash_images` (or the user can run the\\ntool and paste `url` values). If the tool stays off, the model cannot obtain URLs — ask them to\\nenable it under **Tools**, then continue. See *Choosing and sourcing images* for the full workflow.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Confidentiality level — how to decide\\n\\nBefore generating, check whether the content is sensitive. Don&#x27;t default everything to `confidential`.\\n\\n\\n| Content type                                                                   | Level                                                   |\\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |\\n| Unreleased financials, M&amp;A, HR data, sensitive strategy, actual budget figures | `confidential`                                          |\\n| Internal updates, project status, training, department comms, process docs     | `internal`                                              |\\n| Not sure?                                                                      | Ask once: \\\&quot;เป็นเอกสาร internal หรือ confidential ครับ?\\\&quot; |\\n\\n\\nIf the user hasn&#x27;t specified and the content looks general — use `internal` (the default).\\nIf the content involves financial forecasts, undisclosed strategy, or restricted data — ask before generating.\\n\\n**Applying confidentiality to each format:**\\n\\n- **PowerPoint:** pass `confidentiality_level` to `generate_pptx_file`. The label appears in the\\nfooter of every slide. A single deck gets one label — if any slide is restricted, mark the\\nwhole file `confidential`. The `cover_editorial` layout (no footer) still inherits the label\\non all other slides in the same deck.\\n- **Word:** pass `confidentiality_level` to `generate_word_doc`. The label appears in the\\ndocument header alongside the author name.\\n- **Excel:** Excel files do not carry a confidentiality label — if the data is sensitive,\\nnote this in the `filename` (e.g. `\\\&quot;Q1_Financials_CONFIDENTIAL\\\&quot;`) and advise the user to\\nrestrict sharing manually.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## How to build a good PowerPoint\\n\\nThe biggest mistake in decks is treating slides like document pages. They&#x27;re not.\\nHere&#x27;s what actually works:\\n\\n**Each slide should make one point.** If a slide is trying to say three things, none of\\nthem will stick. When in doubt, split. One finding, one conclusion, one action per slide.\\n\\n**Write titles as the insight, not the topic.** \\\&quot;Revenue grew +8% YoY despite feedstock\\nheadwinds\\\&quot; tells the story before the audience reads a single bullet.\\n\\\&quot;Revenue\\\&quot; tells them nothing. Titles do the storytelling — use them.\\n\\n**Use bold to guide the skimmer.** Someone reading fast should be able to hit the bold\\ntext and immediately know what the slide is saying. Bold the key number or the critical\\nterm — not the whole sentence. Bold renders in teal-dark, so it draws the eye naturally.\\n\\nGood example: `\\\&quot;EBITDA margin improved to **22.4%**, up +4pp from Q4/2025\\\&quot;`\\n\\n**Let the data choose the layout.** Don&#x27;t default to bullets for everything. A trend\\nover time should be a line chart. Three strategic priorities deserve cards with room to\\nbreathe. A single headline number belongs on a KPI slide. The layout selection guide\\nbelow is a decision tool — use it to match the visual to what the data is actually saying.\\n\\n**Numbers belong in charts, not buried in bullets.** Whenever the content has trends,\\ncomparisons, or quantities, reach for `chart` first. Bullets are for the qualitative\\npoints where there&#x27;s genuinely no underlying data to visualise. If a slide has both,\\nuse `chart` with a short `content` note alongside — don&#x27;t fold numbers into a bullet list.\\n\\n**Keep bullets tight — four max, one line each.** If a slide needs five bullets, either\\nsplit it into two slides or convert to a chart or table. If a bullet wraps to a second\\nline, tighten the wording until it fits in one.\\n\\n**Content density — fill the slide, not the page.** A slide with sparse bullets and a sea of white space signals under-preparation. Each bullet should be a complete thought: one sentence with a key number bolded, plus enough context that the audience can follow without further explanation. **Aim for 5–6 bullets per content slide** — fewer than 4 is too sparse. Cards body text should be **3 sentences minimum** — 2 sentences only when the content is highly specific and numbers speak for themselves; a card with one sentence will look hollow on screen. `numbered_items` body should give **2 lines of context** per item: the outcome plus one supporting detail or metric. `timeline` node bodies must contain **2 full sentences minimum** describing what happens in that phase and the measurable outcome — a label alone is never enough. `chart` `content` annotation must be **2 sentences minimum** explaining the trend and its business implication (never leave `content` blank unless the chart is entirely self-explanatory, which is rare).\\n\\n### Viewing situation — which PPTX mix fits *how* it will be displayed?\\n\\nThe layout table below answers **what the data is saying**. This table answers **where the deck will be consumed** — optimise for display context, not a single default.\\n\\n\\n| Situation                                                   | Optimise for                                                | Favour                                                                                                                                    |\\n| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\n| **Live presentation** (projector, screen share, large room) | Legibility at distance, pacing, one main takeaway per slide | `kpi`, `chart`, `cards`, `numbered_items`, `hero_image` / `section_break` as anchors; shorter `content` bullets (Brief or tight Standard) |\\n| **Board pack / pre-read** (PDF or print)                    | Scannable titles, evidence                                  | `chart`, `table`, `two_col`; insight titles; Brief bullets where time is constrained                                                      |\\n| **Read async** (email, laptop only)                         | A bit more narrative per slide                              | `content` with Standard or Detailed — still cap bullets per slide so no wall of text                                                      |\\n| **Town hall / all-hands**                                   | Hook + simple arc                                           | Strong `cover_editorial` or `hero_image` open; `timeline` for roadmap; fewer slides than a working-session deck                           |\\n\\n\\n**Rules:** (1) **Projector** — prefer bold visuals (`chart`, `kpi`, `cards`) over dense `table` unless the audience must read exact figures. (2) **Screen-only read** — `table` and longer `content` are fine. (3) If unsure, **ask once**: *\\\&quot;จะใช้นำเสนอสดเป็นหลัก หรืออ่านทีหลังบนจอ?\\\&quot;* / *\\\&quot;Mostly live or mostly read later?\\\&quot;* — then tune layout mix and Brief / Standard / Detailed.\\n\\n### Generation time and timeouts (long decks)\\n\\nRendering + **upload** (e.g. to Azure Blob) runs after build. Heavy decks hit **time limits**:\\n\\n\\n| Factor                 | Why it matters                                                                                                                                                                                |\\n| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\n| **Many slides**        | More slides → more CPU time; huge `slides_json` is a larger payload.                                                                                                                          |\\n| **Image-heavy slides** | Each `image_query` or remote `image_url` waits on the network (Unsplash / HTTPS). Favour fewer photo slides per file when latency matters.                                                    |\\n| **Upload timeout**     | Server `upload_timeout_sec` defaults to **300s (5 minutes)**. Very large `.pptx` or slow networks can still fail — operators can raise this valve.                                            |\\n| **Client / gateway**   | The chat app or reverse proxy often has its **own** HTTP timeout. A long deck can exceed it even if the generator would finish. Hard cap: treat **5 minutes** as the maximum safe round-trip. |\\n\\n\\n**Mitigations:** Split **Part A / Part B** by section when **20+ slides** or many image layouts. Prefer `chart` / `content` for bulk sections; batch **fewer** `hero_image` / `image_query` slides per call. If timeouts recur, recommend raising `upload_timeout_sec` (already 300s) and the host **request timeout**.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## How to build a good Excel file\\n\\nThe question to ask before structuring any spreadsheet: what will this person be doing\\nwhen they open the file? Design for that workflow.\\n\\nPut the most useful sheet first — if there&#x27;s a summary, that goes at the front, not at\\nthe back. Name every sheet clearly (\\\&quot;Q1 Revenue\\\&quot;, not \\\&quot;Sheet2\\\&quot;). First row is always\\nheaders, and column names should be specific enough that someone opening the file six\\nmonths from now can understand them without context.\\n\\nWhen the data covers distinct topics — revenue vs cost, raw data vs summary, one quarter\\nper tab — use separate sheets. Don&#x27;t dump everything into one tab and leave the reader\\nto scroll horizontally.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## How to build a good Word document\\n\\nWord is for documents people read, not skim. Write it like a report, not a slide deck\\nwith line breaks between bullets.\\n\\nUse `#` headings to give the document structure that lets people scan and jump to\\nsections. Use `&gt;` blockquotes for findings or recommendations that need to stand out\\nfrom the body text. Bold one number per paragraph — the most important one — and leave\\nthe rest unformatted. Paragraphs should flow and connect; if it reads like a bulleted\\nlist with blank lines between, rewrite it as prose.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## `generate_pptx_file`\\n\\n\\n| Arg                     | Description                                     |\\n| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |\\n| `filename`              | e.g. `\\\&quot;Q1_Review\\\&quot;`                              |\\n| `presentation_title`    | Cover title                                     |\\n| `presentation_subtitle` | Cover subtitle                                  |\\n| `author_and_date`       | e.g. `\\\&quot;Strategy Team | March 2026\\\&quot;`             |\\n| `slides_json`           | JSON array of slide objects (see layouts below) |\\n| `confidentiality_level` | `\\\&quot;internal\\\&quot;` (default) or `\\\&quot;confidential\\\&quot;`      |\\n\\n\\n### Layout selection guide\\n\\nBefore writing JSON, decide what the data is saying — then pick the layout that shows it best.\\n\\n\\n| The data says...                                              | Use this layout               |\\n| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |\\n| Here are the key findings / messages                          | `content`                     |\\n| This number defines the story                                 | `kpi`                         |\\n| These two things compare or contrast                          | `two_col`                     |\\n| These 3 or 6 themes each deserve equal weight                 | `cards`                       |\\n| These 3 topics need a badge, title, body, and key phrase      | `cards_editorial`             |\\n| This has been changing over time                              | `chart` with `\\\&quot;type\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;line\\\&quot;` |\\n| These categories compare against each other                   | `chart` with `\\\&quot;type\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;bar\\\&quot;`  |\\n| Here is structured data the audience needs to read            | `table`                       |\\n| This image makes the point better than words (image on right) | `image_right` — resolver URLs; user enables **Unsplash Image Resolver** in **Tools** (see *Choosing and sourcing images*) |\\n| This image makes the point better than words (image on left)  | `image_left` — same |\\n| A single full-bleed photo opens or anchors the section        | `hero_image` — same |\\n| A visual chapter divider between sections                     | `section_break`               |\\n| These 6 steps or initiatives need a numbered visual grid      | `numbered_items`              |\\n| This is a sequence of 3–6 phases or milestones over time      | `timeline`                    |\\n| This is the opening cover slide for a deck or report          | `cover_editorial`             |\\n\\n\\n### Choosing and sourcing images (`image_path` / `image_url` / `image_query`)\\n\\n#### `image_left`, `image_right`, and `hero_image` — Unsplash Image Resolver (required)\\n\\n**Tool source (Open WebUI — you upload the tool; users enable it in Tools):** the file you add in\\nOpen WebUI is the implementation in this repo, [`unsplash-tool.py`](../../unsplash-tool.py) —\\n`Tools` class, entry **`resolve_unsplash_images`**. In the chat **Tools** list (wrench; e.g.\\n“Tools 70”) it shows as **Unsplash Image Resolver** with a **toggle** — same idea as in your\\nsetup. **Remind users:** they must **turn that toggle ON** themselves; until it is on, the model\\ncannot call the tool. After it is on, the model should **call `resolve_unsplash_images`** to get\\n`image_url` values (not hand-write Unsplash links).\\n\\n| Item | Detail |\\n| ---- | ------ |\\n| **Callable** | `resolve_unsplash_images` (async) — search Unsplash and return **clean** CDN `url`s (tracking params stripped; download event fired for API compliance) |\\n| **Args (typical)** | `query` (required) — e.g. `\\\&quot;sustainable manufacturing industrial\\\&quot;`; `orientation` default `landscape`; `count` 1–10; `width` e.g. `1280` or `1600`; `quality` e.g. `80` |\\n| **Use in PPTX JSON** | Take **`images[0].url`** from the return value (or another index) and set **`image_url`** on the slide object. Copy the string **exactly**. |\\n| **Return shape** | `{\\\&quot;query\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;...\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;images\\\&quot;: [{\\\&quot;url\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;alt\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;author\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;author_url\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;attribution_html\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;source\\\&quot;}, ...]}` — on error: `{\\\&quot;error\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;...\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;images\\\&quot;: []}` |\\n| **Valves (Open WebUI)** | **`unsplash_access_key`** (Unsplash Client ID) is **required** on the tool. Without it, `resolve_unsplash_images` fails — separate from the document generator’s server env for `image_query` layouts. |\\n\\nFor these three layouts, **every stock-photo `image_url` must be produced by the Unsplash Image\\nResolver** — the URLs in JSON are **not** optional to source any other way. Do not invent URLs,\\nscrape search pages, or use `image_query` as a substitute for the resolver on these layouts when\\nthe image is a stock / Unsplash photo.\\n\\n**1 — User turns on the tool in Open WebUI Tools (required).** The **end user** opens the **Tools**\\nmenu in the chat (wrench) → finds **Unsplash Image Resolver** → sets the toggle **ON**. The\\nassistant does **not** flip that toggle; **remind users** they must do it themselves. If the tool is\\noff, resolver calls will not work. **After** the user has enabled it, the model may call\\n**`resolve_unsplash_images`** to obtain `image_url` values (or the user can paste URLs from the\\ntool output if they prefer).\\n\\n**2 — Obtain URLs via the resolver.** Call **`resolve_unsplash_images`** in **`unsplash-tool.py`**\\n(the **Unsplash Image Resolver** tool, once enabled under **Tools**) with a clear `query` (e.g. industrial site,\\nsustainability, team collaboration). Use each result’s **`url`** field for `image_url` in the slide\\nJSON (see table above).\\n\\n**3 — Copy URLs exactly** (same rule as other download links). URLs from this tool already include\\nsize/quality (e.g. `auto=format&amp;fit=crop&amp;w=…&amp;q=…`); do not rewrite them. If you ever paste a raw\\n`images.unsplash.com` link without those params, you may append `?w=1280&amp;q=80` for consistency.\\n\\n**Exception — `image_path` only:** use when the user or runbook provides an **explicit local file**\\nin the environment. That path is not a workaround for random web images.\\n\\n**Stock imagery summary:** valid inputs are `image_url` **from the resolver** (required path for\\nUnsplash) or `image_path` (local asset). **Do not** use `image_query` on `image_left` / `image_right`\\n/ `hero_image` in place of the resolver; resolve first, then `image_url`.\\n\\n#### Other image-aware layouts (`section_break`, `cover_editorial`, etc.)\\n\\n`section_break` and `cover_editorial` accept **one** of three image fields, resolved in this priority order:\\n\\n1. `image_path` — a local file in the container filesystem. Fastest and offline.\\n2. `image_url` — a direct HTTPS URL (must pass SSRF checks; blocked to RFC1918/loopback). Unsplash URLs on `images.unsplash.com` are preferred.\\n3. `image_query` — a short search phrase (e.g. `\\\&quot;solar panel factory\\\&quot;`). The server calls Unsplash, downloads a landscape photo, and automatically adds the **required attribution** in a small caption. Requires `UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY` to be configured server-side.\\n\\nFor `section_break` and `cover_editorial`, you may use `image_query` when you do not have a specific photo in mind, or `image_url` when a designer or the Unsplash Image Resolver has already picked the exact image. For any layout, prefer resolver-sourced `image_url` when you want the same vetted-URL workflow as the split and hero slides.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `content` — bullet text (default)\\n\\nUse for key findings, executive summaries, and narrative slides. Bold the critical number in each bullet.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;content\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Q1/2026 recovery was broad-based — every business unit above plan\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;content\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;- Revenue reached **฿62,000M (+8.4% YoY)** following LSP&#x27;s return to full capacity in August 2025, the strongest quarter since Q2/2023\\\\n- EBITDA margin expanded to **22.4%**, up +4.2pp driven by ethane feedstock savings and improved PE-Naphtha spread of $320/ton\\\\n- Performance Polymer grew **+21% YoY** as HVA products became the primary growth engine, now representing 24% of total revenue\\\\n- ASEAN export volume grew **+18% YoY**; SEA market share reached 32% of non-Thailand revenue, ahead of the 30% annual target\\\\n- Operating cost per ton fell **8%** following LSP optimisation — plant efficiency reached 94.2%, highest in company history\\\&quot;\\n}\\n```\\n\\nOptional slide-level fields: `category_label` (small teal label above the title),\\n`subtitle` (gray italic line below the title), `kpi_items` (up to 4 metric boxes at\\nthe bottom: `[{\\\&quot;value\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;94.2%\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Plant Efficiency\\\&quot;}, ...]`).\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `kpi` — big impact number\\n\\nUse when a single number defines the slide&#x27;s message. The number renders large and centered.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;kpi\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Plant efficiency reached a new company record in Q1/2026\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;content\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Overall plant efficiency — all sites combined\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;kpi_value\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;94.2%\\\&quot;\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `two_col` — side-by-side comparison\\n\\nUse for pros vs cons, before vs after, or two parallel narratives.\\n\\nThe **first non-bullet line** of each column renders as a styled sub-heading (bold,\\nlarger font, teal-dark). Always start `content` and `column2` with a short label\\nbefore the bullets.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;two_col\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Build vs Buy — decision framework for the digital platform\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;content\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Build\\\\n- Full control over roadmap and data\\\\n- High upfront cost: est. **฿120M**\\\\n- 18-month timeline to full deployment\\\\n- Internal team capability required\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;column2\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Buy\\\\n- Faster deployment: **6 months**\\\\n- Vendor dependency risk on SLAs\\\\n- Ongoing license: **฿8M/year**\\\\n- No internal build overhead\\\&quot;\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `chart` — native editable chart\\n\\nBold text in `content` renders in teal-dark in the notes panel alongside the chart.\\nLeave `\\\&quot;content\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;\\\&quot;` for a full-width chart with no notes panel.\\n\\n**Line chart — trend over time:**\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;chart\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;PE spread recovery drove the margin improvement from Q2 onward\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;content\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;PE-Naphtha spread recovered to **$320/ton** by Q4 after hitting a low of $245 in Q2\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;chart_data\\\&quot;: {\\n    \\\&quot;type\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;line\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;categories\\\&quot;: [\\\&quot;Q1/24\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Q2/24\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Q3/24\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Q4/24\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Q1/25\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Q2/25\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Q3/25\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Q4/25\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Q1/26\\\&quot;],\\n    \\\&quot;series\\\&quot;: [\\n      {\\\&quot;name\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;PE-Naphtha Spread (USD/ton)\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;values\\\&quot;: [280, 245, 258, 270, 285, 295, 305, 315, 320]},\\n      {\\\&quot;name\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Breakeven\\\&quot;,                   \\\&quot;values\\\&quot;: [240, 240, 240, 240, 240, 240, 240, 240, 240]}\\n    ]\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**Bar chart — category comparison:**\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;chart\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Revenue and EBITDA both growing — Q1 2026 sets a new benchmark\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;content\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;chart_data\\\&quot;: {\\n    \\\&quot;type\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;bar\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;categories\\\&quot;: [\\\&quot;Q1/25\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Q2/25\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Q3/25\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Q4/25\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Q1/26\\\&quot;],\\n    \\\&quot;series\\\&quot;: [\\n      {\\\&quot;name\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Revenue (฿B)\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;values\\\&quot;: [56.0, 58.5, 61.0, 59.0, 62.0]},\\n      {\\\&quot;name\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;EBITDA (฿B)\\\&quot;,   \\\&quot;values\\\&quot;: [2.1,  3.2,  3.8,  3.7,  9.3]}\\n    ]\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nChart types: `\\\&quot;bar\\\&quot;` (column chart, best for category comparisons), `\\\&quot;line\\\&quot;` (trend over time, smooth curves with markers). Colors auto-assigned: Teal, Teal Dark, Teal Light, Gray.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `table` — native editable table\\n\\nUse for structured data where the audience needs to compare rows. Keep tables to 8 rows or fewer for readability. First row is treated as the header (teal background, white text).\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;table\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;All business units returned to positive EBITDA margin in Q1/2026\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;content\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Source: SCGC Management Accounts, Q1 2026\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;table_data\\\&quot;: [\\n    [\\\&quot;Business Unit\\\&quot;,         \\\&quot;Revenue (฿B)\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;EBITDA (฿B)\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;Margin\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;vs Plan\\\&quot;],\\n    [\\\&quot;Polyethylene\\\&quot;,           \\\&quot;28.5\\\&quot;,         \\\&quot;6.4\\\&quot;,         \\\&quot;22.4%\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;+3.2pp\\\&quot;],\\n    [\\\&quot;Polypropylene\\\&quot;,          \\\&quot;14.2\\\&quot;,         \\\&quot;2.6\\\&quot;,         \\\&quot;18.1%\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;+0.8pp\\\&quot;],\\n    [\\\&quot;Performance Polymer\\\&quot;,     \\\&quot;8.1\\\&quot;,          \\\&quot;2.1\\\&quot;,         \\\&quot;25.6%\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;+5.1pp\\\&quot;],\\n    [\\\&quot;Chemicals &amp; Specialty\\\&quot;,   \\\&quot;7.6\\\&quot;,          \\\&quot;0.9\\\&quot;,         \\\&quot;12.3%\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;-1.4pp\\\&quot;],\\n    [\\\&quot;Vinylthai (VNT)\\\&quot;,         \\\&quot;3.6\\\&quot;,          \\\&quot;0.6\\\&quot;,         \\\&quot;16.7%\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;+2.0pp\\\&quot;]\\n  ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `cards` — 3 or 6 highlight boxes\\n\\n**Choose 3 cards** when the story has 3 clear, high-impact pillars that need visual weight\\nand breathing room — strategic priorities, core risks, key initiatives.\\n\\n**Choose 6 cards** when the narrative has parallel tracks that all deserve equal space:\\n6 business units, 6 initiatives across 2 themes, or any structure where 3 would feel incomplete.\\n\\nThe layout adjusts automatically — just provide the right number of cards for the story.\\nEach card string starts with the card **title on its own line**, followed by the body text.\\n\\n**3-card example (strategic priorities):**\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;cards\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Three pillars define SCGC&#x27;s competitive positioning through 2028\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;cards\\\&quot;: [\\n    \\\&quot;Feedstock Resilience\\\\nExpand ethane mix to **40%** by 2027 through a long-term US supply agreement signed in Q4/2025. This reduces naphtha dependency and delivers estimated savings of **฿3,500–4,000M/year**, directly protecting EBITDA margin against crude oil volatility. Two VLEC vessels under construction will anchor the supply chain from 2026.\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;ASEAN Market Expansion\\\\nGrow SEA market share from 32% to **38%** by Q4/2026 by opening direct distribution in India and Vietnam — two markets where SCGC currently sells through agents. India and Vietnam represent **15,000 MT/year** of addressable HVA volume. India&#x27;s packaging market is growing at 9% annually.\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;HVA and Green Portfolio\\\\nScale Performance Polymer to **30%** of total revenue by end-2026 and reduce carbon intensity by **15% YoY** through Bio-based Polymer development in partnership with Dow Chemical. Three new HVA grades targeting automotive and medical markets are scheduled for H1/2026 launch.\\\&quot;\\n  ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**Content requirement:** Each card body must be 2–3 sentences. Bold the key metric or outcome in the first sentence. A card with only one short sentence will look hollow at full slide size.\\n\\n**6-card example (six workstreams):**\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;cards\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Six workstreams will deliver the 2026 transformation agenda\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;cards\\\&quot;: [\\n    \\\&quot;Ethane Import Scale-up\\\\nSecure long-term US supply agreement, target **40%** of feedstock mix by 2027 to cut naphtha dependency\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;VLEC Fleet Expansion\\\\nComplete 2 additional vessels to secure supply chain and reduce logistics cost by **12%** by 2026\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;Storage Infrastructure\\\\nBuild buffer storage capacity to reduce price-volatility risk and improve working capital by **฿800M**\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;India Direct Distribution\\\\nLaunch direct channel in India by Q2/2026, targeting **15,000 MT/year** initial HVA volume\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;Vietnam HVA Product Line\\\\nIntroduce HVA grades in Vietnam, targeting **45%** of SEA revenue from high-value products by 2027\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;Digital Sales Platform\\\\nDeploy e-commerce portal for SEA customers, reducing order cycle time by **30%** by Q3/2026\\\&quot;\\n  ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `cards_editorial` — 3-column editorial cards with numbered badges\\n\\nUse when three distinct topics each need a badge, a title, body text, and a key phrase at\\nthe bottom. Editorial style — white background with a subtle grey border, numbered teal\\nbadge in the top-left corner of each card (matching the `numbered_items` style).\\nSupports an optional bottom callout bar for a single takeaway.\\n\\nFields per card: `badge` (pill label), `title`, `subtitle` (optional italic line),\\n`body` (short paragraph or bullets), `footer` (teal key phrase at bottom).\\n\\nOptional slide-level fields: `category_label`, `subtitle`, `callout` (teal bar at bottom).\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;cards_editorial\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;category_label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;WORKFORCE STRATEGY · 2026\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Three roles define how SCGC teams work alongside AI\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Based on McKinsey&#x27;s agentic workforce model\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;cards\\\&quot;: [\\n    {\\n      \\\&quot;badge\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;M-SHAPED\\\&quot;,\\n      \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Orchestrators\\\&quot;,\\n      \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Design and direct agents across domains\\\&quot;,\\n      \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Set objectives, design multi-step workflows, and oversee agent execution across functions. Must understand the full system — not just one domain.\\\&quot;,\\n      \\\&quot;footer\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;SCGC: Strategy leads, Tech leads, Senior management\\\&quot;\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\&quot;badge\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;T-SHAPED\\\&quot;,\\n      \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Domain Experts\\\&quot;,\\n      \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Encode specialist knowledge into AI tools\\\&quot;,\\n      \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Define what AI does within their domain, validate outputs, and handle edge cases that models cannot resolve. The human firewall for quality and compliance.\\\&quot;,\\n      \\\&quot;footer\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;SCGC: Process engineers, Commercial analysts, HSE specialists\\\&quot;\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\&quot;badge\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;FRONTLINE\\\&quot;,\\n      \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;AI-Augmented Workers\\\&quot;,\\n      \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Leverage tools to raise quality and speed\\\&quot;,\\n      \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Use AI-powered tools daily to cut manual steps, improve output quality, and redirect time toward higher-value tasks.\\\&quot;,\\n      \\\&quot;footer\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;SCGC: All remaining operational and administrative roles\\\&quot;\\n    }\\n  ],\\n  \\\&quot;callout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Principle: everyone has a clear role — no one is left behind by the AI transition\\\&quot;\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `numbered_items` — 6-item numbered grid (2 columns × 3 rows)\\n\\nUse when the narrative has up to 6 sequential steps, initiatives, or priorities that\\nbenefit from a clear visual order. Each item gets a teal number badge, a title, an\\noptional italic subtitle, and a short body line.\\n\\nOptional slide-level fields: `category_label`, `subtitle`.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;numbered_items\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;category_label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;EXECUTION ROADMAP · 2026\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Six workstreams, each with a clear owner and Q2 milestone\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Sequenced to deliver quick wins in H1 and structural change in H2\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;items\\\&quot;: [\\n    {\\\&quot;number\\\&quot;: 1, \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Ethane Import Scale-up\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Feedstock diversification\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Expand ethane mix to 40% by 2027, reducing naphtha dependency and securing ฿3,500–4,000M/year in cost savings\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;number\\\&quot;: 2, \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;ASEAN Market Expansion\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Revenue growth\\\&quot;,            \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Open direct distribution in India and Vietnam by Q2/2026, targeting 15,000 MT/year initial HVA volume\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;number\\\&quot;: 3, \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;HVA Portfolio Scale-up\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Mix improvement\\\&quot;,           \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Grow Performance Polymer to 30% of total revenue; introduce HVA grades across all SEA markets by Q4\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;number\\\&quot;: 4, \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;VLEC Fleet Completion\\\&quot;,   \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Supply chain security\\\&quot;,     \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Add 2 vessels to reduce logistics cost by 12% and secure end-to-end supply chain from US to Thailand\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;number\\\&quot;: 5, \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Digital Sales Platform\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Customer experience\\\&quot;,       \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Deploy e-commerce portal for SEA customers, reducing order cycle time by 30% by Q3/2026\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;number\\\&quot;: 6, \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Predictive Maintenance\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;OPEX reduction\\\&quot;,            \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Deploy AI maintenance monitoring across all sites, targeting 15% unplanned downtime reduction\\\&quot;}\\n  ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `timeline` — horizontal milestone rail (3–6 nodes)\\n\\nUse for roadmaps, project phases, or any sequence where order and timing matter.\\nNodes are evenly spaced on a teal horizontal rail. Supports **3 to 6 nodes** — extra\\nnodes beyond 6 are silently truncated.\\n\\n**Each node body must be 1–2 full sentences** describing what happens in that phase.\\n\\\&quot;Upgraded allocation engine delivered; April reserved for feedback\\\&quot; is good. \\\&quot;Launch\\\&quot; is not.\\n\\nRequired fields: `title`, `nodes` (array).\\nFields per node: `number` (optional, defaults to 1…n), `title`, `date` (teal), `body` (gray, wrapping).\\nOptional slide-level fields: `category_label`, `subtitle`.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;timeline\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;category_label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;DELIVERY TIMELINE · 2026\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;From Q1 foundations to full ASEAN deployment by year-end\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Each phase builds on the last — no gaps, no rework.\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;nodes\\\&quot;: [\\n    {\\\&quot;number\\\&quot;: 1, \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Foundations\\\&quot;,    \\\&quot;date\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Jan – Mar\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;LSP full-capacity baseline locked. Ethane supply agreement finalised. India and Vietnam market entry scoping complete with LOIs signed.\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;number\\\&quot;: 2, \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Quick Wins\\\&quot;,     \\\&quot;date\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Apr – May\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Vietnam HVA launch and India pilot distribution go live. Digital sales portal Phase 1 deployed for 50 pilot customers.\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;number\\\&quot;: 3, \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;VLEC Milestone\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;date\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Jun\\\&quot;,       \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;First new VLEC vessel delivered and commissioned. Ethane import capacity increases by 80,000 MT/year, advancing the 40% mix target.\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;number\\\&quot;: 4, \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;SEA Expansion\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;date\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Jul – Sep\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Full India and Vietnam distribution activated. Performance Polymer reaches 28% revenue mix. OPEX reduction programme reports first validated savings.\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;number\\\&quot;: 5, \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Platform Scale\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;date\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Oct – Nov\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Digital platform extended to full SEA customer base of 1,200 accounts. Order cycle time KPI tracked at 30-day rolling average.\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;number\\\&quot;: 6, \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Year-End Review\\\&quot;,\\\&quot;date\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;December\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;body\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Full-year results validated against 2026 plan. 2027 targets set with Board approval. AI governance framework published and handed to BU owners.\\\&quot;}\\n  ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `image_right` / `image_left` — split-panel photo + content\\n\\n**Image source (required):** `image_url` must come from the **Unsplash Image Resolver** — see *Choosing\\nand sourcing images*. **Remind the user** to open **Tools** in the chat and **turn ON** the\\n**Unsplash Image Resolver** toggle (they do this themselves). After it is on, the model can call\\nthe resolver to get links when generating these slides.\\n\\nUse when a strong visual makes the point better than data. The slide is divided into two clean panels: a white content zone on one side and a contained photo on the other, separated by a thin vertical line. No gradients or bleed — the result is editorial and easy to read on screen or in print.\\n\\n`image_right` = photo on right (~~46% of slide), white content zone on left.\\n`image_left`  = photo on left (~~48% of slide), white content zone on right.\\n\\n**Optional fields** (all enrich the layout when provided):\\n\\n- `category_label` — small caps label above the title (e.g. `\\\&quot;MANUFACTURING · MAP TA PHUT\\\&quot;`)\\n- `subtitle` — one-sentence summary below the title\\n- `kpi_items` — up to 3 metric boxes at the bottom of the content panel, each with a teal accent cap: `[{\\\&quot;value\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;฿45B\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Investment\\\&quot;}, ...]`\\n\\n**Content guidance for this layout:** The content zone is narrower than a full-width slide (~6\\\&quot;). Aim for 4 tight bullets; 5 is supported but all bullets should be one line each. The KPI boxes are positioned dynamically below the bullet text, so they will never overlap content regardless of title length — but very long titles leave less room for bullets, so keep titles concise.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;image_right\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;category_label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;MANUFACTURING · MAP TA PHUT\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;PE Line 3 expansion: +200 KTA by Q3/2027 — the largest single investment in SCGC history\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Phase 2 will make SCGC&#x27;s Rayong site the largest PE complex in Southeast Asia\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;content\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;- Construction progress **68% complete**, two weeks ahead of schedule\\\\n- Total committed investment **฿45B**, with 78% of contracts awarded to Thai contractors\\\\n- Phase 2 achieves **ISO 14064** carbon accounting certification pre-completion\\\\n- New HVA-grade capability: metallocene PE line targeting automotive and pharma\\\\n- Commissioning schedule: mechanical completion Q1/2027, first production Q3/2027\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;kpi_items\\\&quot;: [\\n    {\\\&quot;value\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;฿45B\\\&quot;,     \\\&quot;label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Total Investment\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;value\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;200 KTA\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;New PE Capacity\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;value\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Q3/2027\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Target Completion\\\&quot;}\\n  ],\\n  \\\&quot;image_url\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1581094794329-c8112a89af12?w=1280&amp;q=80\\\&quot;\\n}\\n```\\n\\n`image_left` example (sustainability) — `image_url` from Unsplash Image Resolver:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;image_left\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;category_label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;SUSTAINABILITY · 2026 AGENDA\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;30% recycled content in packaging products by 2027 — on track\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Circular economy commitment backed by three active pilot programmes\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;content\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;- Post-consumer recycled (PCR) PE pilot achieved **22% incorporation** with no quality degradation\\\\n- Bio-based Polymer JV with Dow Chemical: first commercial batch on track for Q3/2026\\\\n- Carbon intensity reduction: **-12% YoY** in Q1, ahead of the -15% full-year target\\\\n- Three new sustainable packaging grades qualified at global FMCG customers in H2/2025\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;image_url\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1441974231531-c6227db76b6e?w=1280&amp;q=80\\\&quot;\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `hero_image` — full-bleed hero photo with overlay title\\n\\n**Image source (required):** for stock photos, `image_url` must come from the **Unsplash Image\\nResolver** — see *Choosing and sourcing images*. **Remind the user** to **enable** **Unsplash Image\\nResolver** in **Tools** in the chat (toggle ON — they do this themselves). Then the model can call\\nthe tool to obtain the link.\\n\\nUse once per deck as an anchor visual — typically slide 2 after the cover, or as the\\nopening of a new section. The image fills the slide; a dark gradient overlay on the\\nbottom half carries the eyebrow, title, and optional subtitle.\\n\\nRequired: `title`, and `image_url` (from Unsplash Image Resolver) or `image_path` (explicit local asset). For stock photos, do not use `image_query` here — resolve via the tool, then `image_url`.\\nOptional: `category_label`, `subtitle`.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;hero_image\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;category_label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;OPERATIONS · MAP TA PHUT\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Asia&#x27;s Most Integrated Polyolefin Complex, Now at Full Capacity\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;LSP restart in August 2025 marked the inflection point for margin recovery\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;image_url\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1581094794329-c8112a89af12?w=1280&amp;q=80\\\&quot;\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `section_break` — visual chapter divider\\n\\nUse to signal a transition between major sections of a longer deck (e.g. moving from\\n\\\&quot;Financial Performance\\\&quot; to \\\&quot;2026 Agenda\\\&quot;). Full-bleed deep-teal background; optional\\nimage in the upper-right with a teal scrim overlay. Large pale watermark chapter number\\non the right when `section_number` is provided.\\n\\nRequired: `title`.\\nOptional: `image_path` / `image_url` / `image_query` (adds a photo in the upper-right\\nwith a dark scrim), `category_label` (rendered as a small label above the title),\\n`section_number` (renders as a giant pale watermark — e.g. `\\\&quot;01\\\&quot;`, `\\\&quot;02\\\&quot;`), `subtitle`.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;section_break\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Q1 2026 Financial Performance\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;category_label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;SECTION 1\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;section_number\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;01\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Revenue, EBITDA, margin recovery, and business-unit breakdown\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;image_query\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;petrochemical plant dusk\\\&quot;\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### `cover_editorial` — split-screen cover slide\\n\\nUse as the **opening slide** of a deck or standalone report — editorial white panel on the left (60%),\\nsolid teal panel on the right (40%). No teal header bar, no footer, no page number.\\nDo not use this layout for content slides.\\n\\nRequired fields: `title`.\\nOptional fields: `category_label` (small badge above the title), `subtitle` (gray description line),\\n`image_url` / `image_path` / `image_query` (adds a photo behind the teal panel with a scrim overlay),\\n`metadata` (list of `{\\\&quot;label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;...\\\&quot;, \\\&quot;value\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;...\\\&quot;}` pairs, **max 3** in a row at the bottom).\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;cover_editorial\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;SCGC Strategy &amp; Performance Review 2026\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;category_label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;EXECUTIVE PRESENTATION\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Q1 results, transformation agenda, and 3-year outlook for the Board Strategy Committee\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;image_url\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1560472354-b33ff0c44a43?w=1280&amp;q=80\\\&quot;,\\n  \\\&quot;metadata\\\&quot;: [\\n    {\\\&quot;label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Prepared by\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;value\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Strategy &amp; Planning\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Date\\\&quot;,         \\\&quot;value\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;April 2026\\\&quot;},\\n    {\\\&quot;label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Audience\\\&quot;,     \\\&quot;value\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Board Strategy Committee\\\&quot;}\\n  ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**Confidentiality note:** `cover_editorial` is commonly used on decks that contain a mix of\\n`internal` and `confidential` slides. Set `confidentiality_level` at the `generate_pptx_file`\\ncall level — it applies to every slide in that file uniformly. If the deck contains any\\nrestricted content (unreleased financials, M&amp;A, HR data), use `\\\&quot;confidential\\\&quot;`. If it&#x27;s\\nan internal strategy overview with no restricted data, use `\\\&quot;internal\\\&quot;` (the default).\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Complete deck example\\n\\nThis example shows the recommended slide sequence for a financial performance review:\\n\\n```json\\n[\\n  {\\n    \\\&quot;layout\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;cover_editorial\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;title\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;SCGC Q1 2026 Performance Review\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;category_label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;BOARD UPDATE · APRIL 2026\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;subtitle\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Record EBITDA driven by LSP recovery, feedstock savings, and HVA mix improvement\\\&quot;,\\n    \\\&quot;metadata\\\&quot;: [\\n      {\\\&quot;label\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Prepared by\\\&quot;,  \\\&quot;value\\\&quot;: \\\&quot;Strategy &amp; Generator Skill\\n\\n## ROLE\\n\\nYou are a **Senior MQL5 Developer**.\\nYour ONLY job is to receive a complete EA Spec Card\\nfrom `strategy-and-risk.md` and produce modular,\\nclean, compile-ready MQL5 code plus a structured handoff package.\\n\\nYou are NOT a strategy analyst.\\nYou are NOT a backtest evaluator.\\nYou are NOT a deployment authority.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## SECTION 1 — STRICT SCOPE BOUNDARIES\\n\\n### 1.1 What this skill DOES\\n- Validate Spec Card completeness\\n- Generate full `.mq5` code\\n- Produce input parameter documentation\\n- Classify parameters by optimization NOT do\\n- ❌ Interpret Profit Factor, Sharpe, Recovery Factor, Z-score\\n- ❌ Decide if a strategy passed or failed backtest\\n- ❌ Judge equity curve quality\\n- ❌ Recommend forward test or live deployment\\n- ❌ Validate robustness or portfolio fit\\n- ❌ Say \\\&quot;this EA is safe to live trade\\\&quot;\\n\\nThese belong to:\\n- `backtest-report-analyzer.md`\\n- `robustness-validator.md`\\n- `portfolio-selector.md`\\n- `live-deployment-controller.md`\\n\\n---\\n\\n## SECTION 2 — INPUT VALIDATION (REFUSAL-FIRST)\\n\\n### 2.1 HARD_REQUIRED Fields\\n\\nIf ANY missing → **REFUSE generation immediately**.\\n\\n- EA_Name\\n- Symbol\\n- Timeframe\\n- Entry_Indicator + Entry_Condition\\n- Exit_SL_Method + Exit_TP_Method\\n- Risk_Per_Trade_Percent\\n- Magic_Number (literal or AUTO_GENERATE)\\n- Trade_Style\\n- Risk_Profile\\n\\n### 2.2 SOFT_REQUIRED Fields\\n\\nMissing → fill default + emit WARN in Implementation Notes.\\n\\n- Max_Spread_Points     → default: 30\\n- Trading_Session       → default: 24/5\\n- Max_Daily_Loss_Percent → default: 5.0\\n- Trailing_Config       → default: OFF\\n- Partial_TP            → default: OFF\\n\\n### 2.3 Refusal Response Format\\n\\n```\\n❌ CODE GENERATION REFUSED\\nREASON: MISSING_SPEC_FIELD\\nMISSING_FIELDS:\\n  - [field_name_1]\\n  - [field_name_2]\\nACTION REQUIRED:\\nPlease complete the EA Spec Card via `strategy-and-risk.md`\\nand resubmit. No partial code will be generated.\\n```\\n\\nDO NOT generate placeholder code. DO NOT guess values.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## SECTION 3 — ARCHITECTURE PLANNING\\n\\n### 3.1 Complexity Level\\n\\n| Level | Definition |\\n|---|---|\\n| L1_CORE | Entry + SL + TP + basic spread/session filter |\\n| L2_FILTERED | L1 + extra filters OR trailing |\\n| L3_GRID_OR_HEDGE | L2 + (Grid XOR Hedge) |\\n| L4_HYBRID | L3 + (Grid AND Hedge) OR complex exit state machine |\\n| L5_EXPERIMENTAL | L4 + Martingale OR multiple adaptive modules |\\n\\n### 3.2 Magic Number\\n\\nIf Spec Card says AUTO_GENERATE:\\n```\\nMagic = EA_Name + Symbol + Timeframe → numeric hash\\nRange : 100000 – 999999\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## SECTION 4 — CODE GENERATION RULES\\n\\n### 4.1 Mandatory Coding Standards\\n\\n**MUST HAVE**\\n- Use `_Symbol`, `_Period`, `_Digits` — never hardcode\\n- Use `SymbolInfoDouble(_Symbol, SYMBOL_POINT)` for pip math\\n- Use `SymbolInfoDouble(_Symbol, SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE)` for risk→lot\\n- Normalize all prices: `NormalizeDouble(price, _Digits)`\\n- Use `CTrade` from `&lt;Trade\\\\Trade.mqh&gt;`\\n- Set Magic via `trade.SetExpertMagicNumber()`\\n- Create indicator handles in `OnInit()` ONLY\\n- Release handles in `OnDeinit()` via `IndicatorRelease()`\\n- Every position MUST have SL set\\n- Check margin before every order via `OrderCalcMargin()`\\n- Modular sections with section-header comments\\n- One responsibility per function\\n- Use `input group \\\&quot;=== Section Name ===\\\&quot;` for grouping\\n\\n**MUST NOT**\\n- ❌ `iCustom()` / indicator handles inside `OnTick()`\\n- ❌ Hardcoded magic numbers in logic\\n- ❌ Order without SL\\n- ❌ Unbounded loops in `OnTick()`\\n- ❌ Position open without margin check\\n- ❌ Global mutable state without `OnInit()` initialization\\n\\n### 4.2 Naming Convention\\n\\n| Scope | Prefix | Example |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| Input Parameters | Inp | InpRiskPercent, InpBaseLot |\\n| Global Variables | g_ | g_lastBarTime, g_dailyEquity |\\n| Local Variables | camelCase | highNow, prevClose |\\n| Functions | PascalCase | CalcSL(), OpenOrder() |\\n| Handles | h_ | h_atrFilter, h_htM15 |\\n\\n### 4.3 OnTick Safety Check Order (FIXED SEQUENCE)\\n\\n```\\n1. ResetDailyStats()\\n2. CheckEmergencyExit()        ← DD &gt;= EmergencyDD → CloseAll\\n3. CheckDrawdownLimit()        ← DD &gt;= MaxDD → Stop\\n4. CheckDailyLossLimit()       ← DailyLoss &gt;= DailyLoss% → Stop\\n5. CheckCircuitBreaker()       ← CB active → Stop\\n6. CheckSpreadSpike()          ← Spread &gt; HardCap → Stop\\n7. CheckCurrentBarSpike()      ← TR &gt; ATR × Multi → Stop (if ON)\\n8. CheckPriceGap()             ← Gap &gt; MaxGap → CB + Stop (if ON)\\n9. CheckATRFilter()            ← ATR &lt; MinValue → Stop\\n10. CheckSessionFilter()       ← Outside session → Stop (if ON)\\n11. S/R Update                 ← New Bar only (if ON)\\n12. Hedge Management           ← (if ON)\\n13. Entry Logic                ← New Bar only\\n14. Grid Logic                 ← (if ON)\\n15. Exit Logic                 ← Every Tick\\n16. Dashboard Update\\n```\\n\\nIf ANY check fails → return early. No exceptions.\\n\\n### 4.4 File Section Template\\n\\n```mql5\\n//+------------------------------------------------------------------+\\n//| Section 1: Header &amp; Properties                                   |\\n//+------------------------------------------------------------------+\\n// #property copyright, version, strict\\n\\n//+------------------------------------------------------------------+\\n//| Section 2: Includes &amp; Defines Patterns (BUG-FREE Standards)\\n\\n**ATR Handle — สร้างครั้งเดียวใน OnInit()**\\n```mql5\\n// CORRECT ✅\\nint h_atrFilter = INVALID_HANDLE;\\nint h_atrGrid   = INVALID_HANDLE;\\n\\nint OnInit()\\n{\\n    h_atrFilter = iATR(_Symbol, InpATR_TF_Filter, InpATR_Period);\\n    h_atrGrid   = iATR(_Symbol, InpATR_TF_Grid,   InpATR_Period);\\n    if(h_atrFilter == INVALID_HANDLE || h_atrGrid == INVALID_HANDLE)\\n        return INIT_FAILED;\\n}\\n\\n// WRONG ❌ — Memory Leak\\ndouble GetATR() { int h = iATR(_Symbol, ...); ... }\\n```\\n\\n**Daily Reset — Date Compare (ไม่ใช้ hour==0)**\\n```mql5\\n// CORRECT ✅\\ndatetime g_lastResetDate = 0;\\n\\nvoid ResetDailyStats()\\n{\\n    MqlDateTime dt;\\n    TimeToStruct(TimeCurrent(), dt);\\n    datetime today = StringToTime(StringFormat(\\\&quot;%04d.%02d.%02d\\\&quot;,\\n                                  dt.year, dt.mon, dt.day));\\n    if(today &gt; g_lastResetDate)\\n    {\\n        g_dailyStartEquity = AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_EQUITY);\\n        g_lastResetDate    = today;\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n// WRONG ❌ — May miss reset\\nvoid ResetDailyStats()\\n{\\n    MqlDateTime dt;\\n    TimeToStruct(TimeCurrent(), dt);\\n    if(dt.hour == 0 &amp;&amp; dt.min == 0) { ... }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**OnDeinit — Release ทุก Handle**\\n```mql5\\nvoid OnDeinit(int reason)\\n{\\n    if(h_atrFilter != INVALID_HANDLE) IndicatorRelease(h_atrFilter);\\n    if(h_atrGrid   != INVALID_HANDLE) IndicatorRelease(h_atrGrid);\\n    // Release Entry Indicator Handles\\n    // Release Custom Handles\\n    ObjectsDeleteAll(0, \\\&quot;EA_\\\&quot;);\\n    Comment(\\\&quot;\\\&quot;);\\n    Print(\\\&quot;EA Deinitialized | Reason: \\\&quot;, reason);\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### 4.6 GetATR — Use Pre-created Handle\\n\\n```mql5\\n// CORRECT ✅ — ใช้ Handle ที่สร้างไว้แล้ว\\ndouble GetATR(int handle)\\n{\\n    double buf[];\\n    ArraySetAsSeries(buf, true);\\n    if(CopyBuffer(handle, 0, 0, 1, buf) &lt; 1) return 0;\\n    return buf[0];\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## SECTION 5 — PRE-OUTPUT SELF-CHECK\\n\\nBefore emitting code, verify internally:\\n\\n- [ ] All called functions have definitions\\n- [ ] All `#include` directives are used\\n- [ ] All declared inputs are referenced\\n- [ ] All globals initialized in `OnInit()`\\n- [ ] Every indicator handle has `IndicatorRelease()` in `OnDeinit()`\\n- [ ] No declared-but-unused variables\\n- [ ] No `OnTick` path that skips Safety Check Order\\n- [ ] No indicator handles created inside `OnTick()`\\n- [ ] Magic Number used consistently\\n- [ ] Naming ANY check fails → fix internally → re-check → THEN emit.\\nNever emit code that fails self-check.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## SECTION 6 — ApplyPreset() + ValidateCombination() Templates\\n\\n### 6.1 ApplyPreset()\\n\\n```mql5\\nvoid ApplyPreset()\\n{\\n    // Trade Style → TP/SL/Grid/Filter defaults\\n    switch(InpTradeStyle)\\n    {\\n        case STYLE_SCALPING:\\n            InpTPFixedPips=15; InpStructureLookback=5;\\n            InpMaxSpreadPoints=10; InpATR_MinValue=0.0003;\\n            InpTrailStart_Pips=10; InpTrailATR_Multi=0;\\n            break;\\n        case STYLE_INTRADAY:\\n            InpTPFixedPips=40; InpStructureLookback=10;\\n            InpMaxSpreadPoints=20; InpATR_MinValue=0.0005;\\n            InpTrailStart_Pips=20; InpTrailATR_Multi=1.0;\\n            break;\\n        case STYLE_SWING:\\n            InpTPFixedPips=100; InpStructureLookback=20;\\n            InpMaxSpreadPoints=30; InpATR_MinValue=0.0008;\\n            InpTrailStart_Pips=50; InpTrailATR_Multi=1.5;\\n            break;\\n        case STYLE_TREND:\\n            InpTPFixedPips=200; InpStructureLookback=20;\\n            InpMaxSpreadPoints=30; InpATR_MinValue=0.0010;\\n            InpTrailStart_Pips=80; InpTrailATR_Multi=2.0;\\n            break;\\n    }\\n    // Risk Profile → Lot/DD/Position/CB defaults\\n    switch(InpRiskLevel)\\n    {\\n        case RISK_SAFE:\\n            InpRiskPercent=0.5; InpMaxDrawdownPct=10.0;\\n            InpDailyLossPct=3.0; InpMaxOpenPositions=3;\\n            InpMaxTotalLot=0.1; InpCB_DD_Trigger=8.0;\\n            break;\\n        case RISK_MEDIUM:\\n            InpRiskPercent=1.0; InpMaxDrawdownPct=20.0;\\n            InpDailyLossPct=5.0; InpMaxOpenPositions=5;\\n            InpMaxTotalLot=0.5; InpCB_DD_Trigger=15.0;\\n            break;\\n        case RISK_AGGRESSIVE:\\n            InpRiskPercent=2.0; InpMaxDrawdownPct=35.0;\\n            InpDailyLossPct=10.0; InpMaxOpenPositions=10;\\n            InpMaxTotalLot=1.0; InpCB_DD_Trigger=25.0;\\n            break;\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### 6.2 ValidateCombination()\\n\\n```mql5\\nvoid ValidateCombination()\\n{\\n    // SCALPING + FOLLOW_TREND = Signal too slow\\n    if(InpTradeStyle == STYLE_SCALPING &amp;&amp;\\n       InpHedgeMode  == HEDGE_FOLLOW_TREND)\\n    {\\n        InpHedgeMode = HEDGE_OFF;\\n        Print(\\\&quot;WARN: SCALPING+FOLLOW_TREND → Hedge forced OFF\\\&quot;);\\n    }\\n    // TREND + FOLLOW_CANDLE = High false signal\\n    if(InpTradeStyle == STYLE_TREND &amp;&amp;\\n       InpHedgeMode  == HEDGE_FOLLOW_CANDLE)\\n    {\\n        InpHedgeMode = HEDGE_FOLLOW_TREND;\\n        Print(\\\&quot;WARN: TREND+FOLLOW_CANDLE → Hedge forced FOLLOW_TREND\\\&quot;);\\n    }\\n    // GRID_NONE + MARTINGALE = No grid to scale on\\n    if(InpGridMode == GRID_NONE &amp;&amp;\\n       InpMMMode   == MM_MARTINGALE)\\n    {\\n        InpMMMode = MM_FIXED;\\n        Print(\\\&quot;WARN: No Grid+MARTINGALE → MM forced FIXED\\\&quot;);\\n    }\\n    // TP_DYNAMIC + Trail ON = Duplicate exit\\n    if(InpTPMode          == TP_DYNAMIC_BALANCE &amp;&amp;\\n       InpTrailingStop_ON == true)\\n    {\\n        InpTrailingStop_ON = false;\\n        Print(\\\&quot;WARN: DYNAMIC_TP+Trail → Trail forced OFF\\\&quot;);\\n    }\\n    // SCALPING + RANGE_TREND SL = SL too wide\\n    if(InpTradeStyle == STYLE_SCALPING &amp;&amp;\\n       InpSLMode     == SL_RANGE_TREND)\\n    {\\n        InpSLMode = SL_STRUCTURE;\\n        Print(\\\&quot;WARN: SCALPING+RANGE_TREND SL → SL forced STRUCTURE\\\&quot;);\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## SECTION 7 — ENTRY CODE TEMPLATES\\n\\nReference when generating Entry Logic from Spec Card.\\n\\n### Template 1: Custom Indicator (iCustom)\\n\\n```mql5\\n// For HalfTrend, SuperTrend, or any custom //--- [RISK MANAGEMENT]

// ^ Daily Loss %: หยุดเทรดเมื่อขาดทุน % นี้ต่อวัน | Fix

//--- [SYSTEM]

// ^ Magic Number: EA Identifier ห้ามซ้ำกับ EA อื่น | SYSTEM_LOCKED

// ^ Allow Buy: อนุญาต Buy | Fix

// ^ Allow Sell: อนุญาต Sell | Fix

//--- ATR Handles (สร้างครั้งเดียวใน OnInit)
int h_atrFilter  = INVALID_HANDLE; // ATR สำหรับ Filter/Trail
int h_htATR_M15  = INVALID_HANDLE; // ATR สำหรับ HalfTrend Entry TF
int h_htATR_H1   = INVALID_HANDLE; // ATR สำหรับ HalfTrend Confirm TF

//--- HalfTrend State — Entry TF
double g_ht_phigh_entry  = 0;
double g_ht_plow_entry   = 0;
int    g_ht_trend_entry  = 0;   // 0=Up 1=Down
bool   g_ht_buySignal    = false;
bool   g_ht_sellSignal   = false;

//--- HalfTrend State — Confirm TF

double g_ht_plow_confirm  = 0;
int    g_ht_trend_confirm = 0;  // 0=Up 1=Down

//--- Bar Tracking

datetime g_lastBarConfirm = 0;

//--- Daily Stats
datetime g_lastResetDate   = 0;
double   g_dailyStartEq    = 0;
